issues.description: Class name and file contents mismatch: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/embedded package and class text inside a method (malformed Java), and the helper singFarmSongVerse has its Animal parameter commented out. The problem statement (UML and tasks) and the solution expect a public class named Farm in the same file, with a private List<Animal> animals, a no-argument constructor that initializes the ArrayList, getters/setters, methods addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), and a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The malformed template (wrong class name, duplicated package/class tokens, commented parameter) causes compilation errors and prevents students from implementing or testing the required methods and following the exercise (they cannot create/compile a Farm class or run Main against it).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a syntactically correct public class Farm matching the exercise specification: ensure file begins with 'package de.tum.cit.ase;', declare 'public class Farm', include 'private List<Animal> animals;', provide a no-arg constructor that sets animals = new ArrayList<>(); add public getter and setter for animals, implement public void addAnimal(Animal animal) to add to the list, implement public void feedAllAnimals() to call and print messageOnFeed() for each Animal, implement public void singFarmSong() that iterates animals and calls a private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) helper. Remove the embedded duplicate package/class text and uncomment/restore the Animal parameter in singFarmSongVerse so the template compiles and aligns with the problem statement and solution while preserving the intended student tasks.

issues.description: The exercise concept 'Farm' is referred to as 'Farm' in the problem statement (UML and tasks) but the template source file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares the class as 'AnimalFarm', while the reference solution implements a class named 'Farm'. Specifically: problem statement expects a class named 'Farm'; template defines public class AnimalFarm (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, line 3); solution defines public class Farm (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, line 6). This naming mismatch prevents students from mapping the requirement to the starter code and will likely cause compilation errors and confusion (e.g., Main references new Farm()).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class declared in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' so the class name matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the public class name matches the filename (Farm.java) and update any internal references accordingly (e.g., Main usage). Alternatively, replace the template file with the solution's Farm.java implementation to provide a correct starter.
